definition: Commensal means relating to a biological relationship in which one organism benefits while the other is neither helped nor harmed.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word commensal. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know commensal should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Cattle egrets have a commensal relationship with grazing buffalo: the birds feast on insects the herd stirs up, and the buffalo gain nothing and lose nothing.
A neutral relationship leaves both species exactly as they were, while a commensal one gives a clear advantage to one of them.
A commensal partner takes its benefit without costing the other anything, but an exploitative one takes that benefit directly at the other's expense.

Coexisting says only that two species live alongside each other without conflict; it makes no claim about who gains or loses. Commensal is a precise verdict on that ledger: one organism benefits while the other is neither helped nor harmed. Pigeons and sparrows coexist on a plaza; the remora riding a shark is commensal.

Cohabiting means sharing the same living space with another organism - two species under one roof, in one burrow, on one reef. It describes the address, not the accounting. Commensal describes the accounting: one partner gains while the other is neither helped nor harmed. Owls and squirrels may cohabit one hollow trunk whether or not either profits.

A remora fastens itself to the underside of a shark with a suction disc on top of its head.
It rides along for weeks, snapping up scraps that drift loose whenever the shark feeds.
The shark's swimming, hunting, and health are unchanged; it appears not to register the passenger at all.
Biologists call this arrangement commensal because exactly one animal profits and the other simply carries on.
One organism (the remora) gains food while the other (the shark) is neither helped nor harmed, which is precisely what commensal describes.

Commensal almost always modifies a relationship, a species, or an organism, as in 'a commensal relationship' or 'commensal bacteria.' Save it for cases where exactly one partner gains and the other is genuinely unaffected; if both partners gain, the word you want is mutualistic.

On the Kansas prairie, burrowing owls raise their chicks underground in holes they never dug.
The digging is done by prairie dogs, which abandon tunnels every season as the colony shifts.
Ecologists describe the arrangement as commensal: the owls gain a ready-made home, while the prairie dogs, long gone from the borrowed tunnels, are neither helped nor harmed.
It is not a friendship -- the two species barely meet -- and it is not theft, since nothing of value is taken from an animal that has moved on.
One side simply profits from the other's leftovers, at no one's expense.
